answer: A reputation graph can resist Sybils if each identity is a vertex whose trust grows only through verified, useful work attested by independent peers. New vertices start at the nadir of influence, with no voting or payout weight, and must accumulate a diverse grove of attestations over time, not a burst from one clique. An attacker must therefore pay the full time and compute cost of doing real work for every fake identity, while cheap mass creation buys no influence, because unconnected or mutually attesting clusters are discounted.
